transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I came in because things have just... gotten really out of hand at work, and I can't keep up anymore. I'm a production manager, and for a while there, I was just going non-stop. I was launching all these massive plant redesign projects, calling our suppliers way after hours, and I even completely rewrote the entire shift plan by myself. I just had so much drive to get it all done. But then, suddenly, I just crashed. Now I can't even keep up with the very plans I set in motion, and it's really starting to affect my job.
Did you feel abnormally happy or on top of the world during the time you were launching those projects and rewriting the shift plan?

Yeah, I did. At the beginning of all those assignments, I felt... almost electrically upbeat. Just completely on top of things. But then it turned into me being weirdly irritable. Like, if anyone questioned my ideas or the new shift plan, I got really frustrated because I felt like they were just slowing down something that was obvious and important.
Are you currently feeling sad or empty most of the day?

Yeah, I do. Lately, I just wake up in the temporary apartment with this really heavy, hollow feeling. It's just there all day. It honestly feels like the day is already ruined before I even get in my car to drive to the plant.
Do you find yourself no longer enjoying activities that you used to find pleasurable?

I don't think so. I haven't really noticed a change with that. I still enjoy my usual hobbies and the things I normally like doing when I actually have time for them. It's just... yeah, I haven't lost interest in them.
Have you been feeling anxious or on edge lately?
No, not really. I haven't noticed feeling anxious or nervous. It's really just that heavy, hollow feeling I mentioned before, but I wouldn't say I feel on edge about anything.
How long have you been feeling this heavy, hollow feeling?

It's been about three months now. This heavy stretch has just been with me for a solid three months. Um, I think with the recent move and the new assignment at the plant, it's just... it's made it a lot harder to manage.
Did you experience any periods where you didn't need much sleep, yet you still felt rested and had a lot of energy?

Yeah, actually, I did. There was a period before this heavy feeling started where... well, I was sleeping maybe two or three hours a night. But I wasn't tired at all. I was still showing up at the plant feeling completely sharp and charged. It honestly just felt like sleep was optional, or just kind of an inefficient use of my time.
Have you noticed any decrease in your interest in activities that usually bring you pleasure over the past three months?

Yeah, definitely. I used to really look forward to going hiking on the weekends, or even just working on some of the woodworking projects I have set up in the garage. But... I haven't touched any of it in months. I just don't see the point right now. I'd rather just sit on the couch. It's like the enjoyment has just been drained out of everything.
Do you feel guilty about anything?

No, not really. I mean, I know I'm not doing much around the house or... or keeping up with my friends, but I don't really feel guilty about it. I just feel... empty. Like I don't have the energy to even care that I'm not doing those things.
Have you noticed yourself moving more slowly or feeling like it's harder to get started on things lately?

Yeah, I have. Actually, people at work have started noticing it, too. Sometimes I'm moving just... painfully slowly. Like it takes a ridiculous amount of effort just to reach over and pick up a binder off my desk. 

But then other times, it's the exact opposite. I'll just be pacing around the production office, picking at my nails constantly, because sitting still just feels completely unbearable.
Have you experienced periods where you felt both really down and extremely energetic or irritable at the same time?

No, I don't think so. When I'm feeling down, like I am now, I just feel completely drained and empty. I don't get those bursts of energy at the same time. The pacing and feeling restless... that just happens sometimes when I'm feeling low, but it's not like I actually have energy. It's just an uncomfortable feeling.
Have you had any thoughts of death or suicidal ideation during these past three months?

No, I haven't. I mean, I feel really empty and drained, like I said, but I haven't had any thoughts about dying or... or hurting myself or anything like that. It's just a lack of energy, not wanting to end things.
Have you lost interest in activities that you usually enjoy?

No, I haven't really noticed that. I mean... I still want to do the things I normally enjoy. It's just that, like I said, I'm so drained it's hard to actually get up and do them sometimes. But the actual interest in them hasn't gone away.
Have you experienced significant weight loss or gain over the past three months?

I haven't really been tracking my exact weight, but my eating habits are just all over the place right now. Some days I'll look at the clock and realize it's 4 p.m. and all I've had all day is coffee. But then other nights... I'll just stand in the kitchen eating takeout straight from the container, even though I'm not actually hungry. It's just very inconsistent.
Have you experienced any unusual thoughts or heard any voices that others couldn't hear during these past three months?
No, I haven't. I mean, my head feels a bit foggy sometimes just from being so exhausted, but... no, I haven't heard any voices or had any thoughts that don't make sense. Nothing like that.
Have you experienced any periods during the past three months where you felt both extremely low and also had bursts of energy or irritability at the same time?

No, I haven't noticed anything like that. When I feel low, I'm just... completely drained, like I mentioned before. I don't really get bursts of energy at the same time. I mean, I might be a little irritable here and there, but I think that's mostly just from being so tired all the time. It's definitely not a burst of energy.
Have you ever felt extremely high and extremely low at the same time?
No, I haven't. Like I said, when I'm down, I'm just completely exhausted and flat. I don't think I've ever felt both extremes at the exact same time. It's usually one or the other.
Was there a specific time when you felt abnormally happy or upbeat that lasted for several days or more before you started feeling down?

Yeah, actually. Right when this current assignment started, I felt... I don't know, almost electrically upbeat for a few days. Like I was totally wired and on top of everything. But then it kind of shifted into feeling weirdly irritable. Like, if anyone questioned my ideas or the production schedule, I just felt like they were slowing down something that was obvious and important. It was a really intense few days before I crashed into feeling so exhausted.
Did you experience any periods where you felt both extremely happy and extremely irritable at the same time, shifting back and forth between the two?

No, not at the same time. It didn't really shift back and forth like that. Like I was saying, it was more of a progression. I started out feeling really great and on top of things, and then... it just kind of morphed into being irritable. But I don't remember feeling both of those things in the exact same moment.
Did you notice that after feeling extremely upbeat and energetic, you then shifted into feeling extremely low, and has this kind of pattern happened more than once?

I'm not really sure. I mean, I definitely crashed this time, like I mentioned. But as for it being a pattern... I haven't really noticed if it always happens in that exact order, or if I've gone from that upbeat feeling straight into a low like this more than once before. I just know how exhausted I am right now.
